certificates.startupTrustBody:
Piper's HTTPS inspection certificate is not trusted by Windows.

Click OK to install Piper's root certificate for this Windows user and restart Piper. HTTPS capture will then work immediately.

This is a security-sensitive change: anything with access to Piper's private key can impersonate HTTPS sites to this Windows account. Only continue on a machine you control.

certificates.trustBody:
Add the Piper root certificate to your user's Trusted Root store?

This is required to inspect HTTPS traffic, and it is a real security tradeoff: anything holding the matching private key - which is stored unencrypted in your user profile - can impersonate any HTTPS site to this Windows account.

Only do this on a machine you control, and use Tools > Remove trusted root certificate when you are finished.

searchHelp.caption: Search syntax
searchHelp.body:
The same query grammar works in Find Sessions, the session filter box and the
Composer search. Terms are combined with AND.

Ctrl+F opens Find Sessions: it marks matching sessions in a colour you pick and
hides nothing. F3 selects the next match. Ctrl+Shift+F focuses the filter box,
which does hide the sessions that do not match.

  checkout               substring across URL, headers and text bodies
  "exact phrase"         quoted literal
  /orders\/[0-9]+/       regular expression

  method:POST            also m:
  method:GET|POST        alternatives
  host:api.example.com   also h:
  domain:example.com     that host and its subdomains, also d:
  path:/v2/users
  url:token
  status:404             also s:
  status:4xx             class shorthand
  status:>=400           comparisons: > >= < <=
  status:200..299        ranges
  status:4xx|5xx         alternatives
  ct:json                content type

  header:Authorization   name or value, request or response
  header:Accept=json     specific header, specific value
  reqheader: respheader: restrict to one side

  body:user_id           either body
  req:  resp:            restrict to one side

  size:>100kb            response size; b/kb/mb/gb suffixes
  reqsize:>0
  dur:>500               duration in milliseconds
  id:1234

  is:https  is:http  is:tunnel  is:composed  is:captured
  is:error  is:ok  is:redirect  is:pending  is:complete
  is:json  is:xml  is:html  is:image  is:script  is:css
  is:slow  is:cached  is:body

  -host:cdn.example.com  negate any term with - or !

An unrecognised field is searched literally, so a pasted URL works as typed.

Example:
  method:POST host:api status:>=400 -is:image body:"order"

filters.helpBody:
Add one or more host patterns, then use their checkboxes to choose which ones apply. Host and Response Status Code edits stay staged, so a partly-typed pattern is never applied on its own.

A full domain or address, such as example.com, *.example.com or 10.0.0.1, matches that host and its subdomains, never a lookalike such as evil-example.com. A fragment matches any host that contains it: a single word (curseforge, localhost, api.) or a partial address (192.168.1). A trailing dot on a full domain, as in example.com., changes nothing.

The Use Filters checkbox takes effect immediately in both directions. Checking it runs the staged filterset straight away, exactly as Actions > Run Filterset now does; unchecking it stops filtering at once, as does Actions > Show all sessions, which leaves the filterset itself intact.

Right-clicking a session and choosing "Hide this host" hides it in the capture list right away and adds it here, so the choice is remembered. Untick or remove the entry and the host shows again at once. Like the rest of the filterset, the saved list takes over once the filterset runs: tick "Use Filters" to keep hiding it. While this list is showing only specific hosts it cannot also carry an exception, so a hide then lasts for the session only; the Log says so, and "Show hosts hidden this session" on the right-click menu undoes it.

Filtered-out sessions are dropped rather than hidden, so traffic captured while a filter is applied cannot be recovered by turning the filter off afterwards. Check your host and status choices before enabling the filterset.

Filters compose into the same query grammar as the session grid's own filter box, but apply separately: running a filterset leaves whatever you typed there alone, and both narrow the list together. Editing that box does not turn the filterset off -- use the Use Filters checkbox for that.

Only Hosts and Response Status Code filters are implemented.

autoResponder.helpBody:
Rules are checked from the top down; the first enabled rule that matches wins.

Match
  orders                     part of the URL, ignoring case
  EXACT:https://host/path    the whole URL, case-sensitive
  NOT:orders                 everything the rest does not match
  REGEX:/v(?<n>\d+)/items    a regular expression, with ${n} usable in the action
  METHOD:POST                the request method
  HEADER:X-Env=staging       a request header
  URLWithBody:coupon         the URL and the request body together
  Q:method:POST host:api     Piper's own filter grammar, request fields only

Action
  *404, *503, *200           answer with that status
  C:\mocks\orders.json       serve that file, content type from its extension
  *inline                    serve the Body box below
  *raw:C:\path\captured.txt  serve a complete saved response, headers included
  *redir:https://other/path  send the client a 307 redirect
  https://other/path         fetch that instead, without telling the client
  *delay:500                 pause, then carry on. Combine: *delay:500 *503
  *drop, *reset              kill the connection
  *CORSPreflightAllow        answer an OPTIONS preflight permissively

Rules cannot see traffic inside an undecrypted HTTPS tunnel. If a rule never fires for
an HTTPS host, check Tools > Configurations > HTTPS.

configurations.caption: Configurations
configurations.savedForFutureSessions: These settings are saved for future Piper sessions.
configurations.captureScopeNote: Capture scope controls which sessions are collected and shown.
configurations.wheelZoomNote: View > Zoom and Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus / Ctrl+0 keep working either way, so turning this off only stops the size changing while you scroll.
configurations.decryptHttpsNote: Requires the Piper root certificate to be trusted.
configurations.http2DownstreamNote: Applies to new decrypted browser connections.
configurations.http3UpstreamNote: Origins are tried over QUIC only after advertising HTTP/3 through Alt-Svc.
configurations.validateUpstreamNote: Off accepts any origin certificate (self-signed, expired, hostname mismatch) -- only for testing a known origin. It also hides a real attacker impersonating that origin.
configurations.analyticsEnabledNote: Sends which features you use, the type of any error, and the app version, tied only to a random ID stored on this machine, over HTTPS to analyticsnew.overwolf.com. Sending is a web request, so it reveals your IP address and when you used Piper. Never sends captured traffic, URLs, hostnames, headers, bodies, cookies, certificates, or your settings. Turning this off also deletes the identifiers it reports with and discards anything not yet sent.
configurations.pendingFeedbackNote: Reports wait in a plain text file you can read before they are sent.

analyticsConsent.caption: Help improve Piper
analyticsConsent.heading: Would you like to send anonymous feedback?
analyticsConsent.intro: Piper is easier to improve when we can see which features get used and what breaks. This is entirely optional, and nothing is collected unless you choose to send it.
analyticsConsent.sentBullets:
•  Which features you use, and how a capture or certificate step turned out
•  The type of any error, with the top few stack frames
•  Piper's version and your Windows version
•  A random ID stored on this machine, deleted if you turn this off
•  Sent over HTTPS to analyticsnew.overwolf.com, run by Overwolf
analyticsConsent.neverBullets:
•  Captured traffic of any kind - URLs, hostnames, headers, bodies, cookies
•  Credentials, certificates, or private keys
•  File paths, error messages, or anything you typed
•  Your settings, rules, or saved sessions
analyticsConsent.notes:
Piper's reporting can only send short words from a fixed list, so captured traffic cannot be included even by mistake. Reports wait in a plain text file you can read before they are sent.

"Anonymous" means the reports carry nothing that identifies you. Sending them is still a web request, so it reveals your IP address and when you were using Piper, the same as visiting a website would.
analyticsConsent.changeLater: You can change this at any time under Tools > Configurations > Privacy.
